explanations: Verb first + subject: Äter du is the yes/no pattern.
Du äter is statement order, even with a question mark.
Äter du inte adds a negation not asked for.
prompt: Build the yes/no question “Do you eat?”

explanations: Var + bor + du: question word, verb, subject.
Du before bor breaks question order.
Vad asks what, but this asks where.
Vad + äter + du keeps verb right after the question word.
Du before äter is statement order.
Var asks where, but this asks what.
In questions inte follows the subject: Äter du inte.
Inte before du splits the verb from its subject.
Du äter inte is the statement, not the question.
prompt: Build the negative question “Do you not eat?”

explanations: Läser hon inte: verb + subject + inte.
Inte before hon is wrong in questions.
Hon läser inte is the statement order.
Varför + äter + du + inte: question word, verb, subject, negation last.
Inte before du is wrong.
Du before äter breaks question order.
Vem + kommer + idag: question word, verb, then time.
Kommer vem idag reverses question word and verb.
Vem idag kommer puts the verb last.
När + äter + vi: question word, verb, subject.
Vi before äter is statement order.
När vi äter breaks the verb-second rule.
Hur + mår + du is the fixed greeting-question order.
Du before mår is statement order.
Vad asks what, not how someone feels.
Vad + läser + hon + inte places inte after the subject.
Inte before hon splits verb and subject.
Hon before läser breaks question order.
